title: 1959 AHSME Problem 30
statement: \(A\) can run around a circular track in \(40\) seconds. \(B,\) running in the opposite direction, meets \(A\) every \(15\) seconds. What is \(B\)’s time to run around the track, expressed in seconds?

solutions.text:
If \(B\)’s lap time is \(t,\) their relative speed is \[ \frac1{40}+\frac1t=\frac1{15}. \] Thus \(\frac{1}{t}=\frac{1}{24},\) so \(t=24\) seconds.

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Measure each runner’s speed in laps per second
Because they run in opposite directions, their speeds add to \(\frac{1}{15}\) lap per second
